# Review - PR 507 @ 55e573949537f392c6e0d427af1dca6783d2474c

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: 2706eeec18394f5bbe022b2874ff2c8bb5dad446. Local-tooling change only (10 files, +1124/-26 against merge base 92b252ed): a reviewed merge train (`local/bin/pr_train.py`), a non-publishing `--integration-head` mode in `ci.sh`, member-ref leasing in `checked-push.sh`, a frozen-base variant of merge gate 2b, protocol/telemetry prose, and 484 lines of new fixture tests.

## Findings

- none

## Review

Scope: no Lean, blueprint, `references/` or `docs/paper-gaps/` file is touched, so the faithfulness policy, the A1-A6 anti-patterns and the proof-frontier rules have no surface in this diff; `rg` over the diff finds no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`. The exact-head status roll-up is green: `local-ci/summary` success at 2026-09-17T13:54:57Z with all eight step contexts success. The PR worktree HEAD equals the published head, so the diff I read is the published one.

Prior ledger (canonical review `5194195608` at `26ecf158`) carried two unresolved findings; both are resolved at this head.

F1 (`checked-push.sh:157`, blocker: only `main` was leased, so a member ref could move after verification and stale member content still be published). `verify_manifest` now returns the member refs it confirmed (`pr_train.py:104-137`) and `--members-out` writes them for the transport (`pr_train.py:290-297`). `checked-push.sh:144-197` validates each row (`refs/heads/` prefix, `check-ref-format`, 40-hex object id, no collision with the published ref, no duplicate ref, at least two members) and then pushes `--atomic` with one `--force-with-lease=<member>:<verified sha>` per member alongside the `main` lease, each member also pushed back at its verified value. A member that moved makes the lease stale, and git 2.34's `reject_atomic_push` aborts the whole transaction client-side before any ref is sent, so `main` is not published either; a member that did not move is up to date and is never rewound. `test_member_moving_at_transport_start_refuses` (`scripts/tests/test_pr_train.py:268-292`) is a real end-to-end exercise of this: a `git` shim moves `refs/heads/issue-3` on the fixture remote at the moment the push starts, and the test asserts non-zero exit, remote `main` still at base, the member keeping its racing value, "rejected" on stderr, `publication.json` outcome `refused`, and no non-GET GitHub call. That is the "test for movement at transport start" the prior round asked for. `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` is refused when `--train-manifest` is given (`checked-push.sh:85`), so the train cannot take the bypass path. The new `EXIT` trap at `checked-push.sh:154` clobbers no earlier trap (there is none).

F2 (`pr_train.py:171`, private telemetry lock). `record()` now writes through `telemetry.append_jsonl` and `telemetry.append_event_bullet` (`pr_train.py:181-204`); `telemetry.py:478-485` takes the canonical `events-md` named lock and the dated-section path, so a concurrent canonical writer can no longer truncate or lose the train event. The `train-telemetry` lock is retained only to serialise trains against each other and the code says so. An unreadable build spool is kept for the operator rather than deleted.

Checked beyond the ledger. `ci.sh --integration-head` sets `FORCE_ALL=1`, rejects `--only`/`--skip-build`/a PR argument, requires 40-hex head and base plus `--worktree`, and re-asserts head identity, cleanliness and base ancestry before and after the run; because `--base` is set the run is `PARTIAL=1`, so it publishes no statuses, no summary and no manifest comment, and its manifest lands at `pr<PR_ID>-<sha>.partial.json`, which is exactly the path `pr_train.ci_path` reads. `check_combined_ci` re-reads that manifest and requires head, merge base, worktree, conclusion and every one of `pr_merge.CI_STEPS` to be `success` with no extra or missing step, so a partial manifest cannot certify a subset. The narrower build command is not a weakening: `lakefile.toml` has `defaultTargets = ["MIPStarRE"]`, so bare `lake build` and `lake build MIPStarRE` cover the same targets, and the axiom audit is added in the same invocation. Passing `--no-build` to `warm-worktree.sh` removes only the cold-path `full_build`, which would otherwise be a nested attempt at the machine-wide lock `ci.sh` already holds at line 1093; the full build stays under `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`. Gate 2b's train branch (`pr_merge.py:483-499`) is strictly stricter than the ordinary predicate - it tolerates no base movement at all, not even passive telemetry - and the three new `MergeGateTests` cases are purely additive. Commit conventions hold: `type(scope): imperative` subjects under 72 characters, the `[codex-review-fix]` prefix spelled exactly, a bracket-free branch name, and a body with Motivation, Description, Testing.

I ran `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_pr_train -v` in the PR worktree with `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` redirected to a private directory: 21 tests, all pass in 78s, all GitHub and git endpoints fixtures.

Two non-blocking observations, neither a defect I would hold the merge for. (a) The `verify_manifest` docstring says "the remote must enforce that they still are when it commits"; the enforcement is in fact a lease evaluated against the ref advertisement, and a member that did not move stays out of the server-side transaction, so the residual advertisement-to-commit window is not closed. `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` states this accurately, and no git ref protocol offers a check-only command, so the docstring is the only place that reads stronger than the mechanism. (b) `pr_merge.py:489` reports "main changed from the frozen integration base" for both a moved base and a base that is not `main` at all; `test_train_rejects_non_main_base` asserts that conflated message, which would misdirect an operator in the second case.

Not verified: no live train was run and no publication path exercised against the real remote (correctly out of scope for a read-only reviewer); the `ci.sh` integration path was exercised only through the fixture tests, not against a real Lean build; I did not re-derive the green `local-ci` steps, I read their published statuses.

Prose lane is n/a: the diff's prose is process documentation (`local/protocols/`, `results/telemetry/events.md`), not blueprint TeX, paper-gap notes or mathematical audits. I did check that the `EVOLUTION.md` and `issues-prs.md` entries describe the mechanism this head actually implements, and they do.

VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=n/a)
